title: The voice in your head is not always your friend.
paragraphs: The voice in your head is not always your friend.
Sometimes… it’s the very thing pulling you away from God.

You hear it when you’re alone.
When the noise dies down.
When no one is watching.
Because that voice keeps whispering things that God never said.
And deep down… you know something is off.

It tells you to stay silent about your sin.
It tells you to delay repentance.
It tells you that “it’s not that serious.”
But the longer you listen… the heavier your soul feels.
And the louder that other voice gets.
Because some of you are being discipled… not by the Holy Spirit—

That voice says:
“Just this once won’t hurt.”

So you click.
You hide.
You justify.

But instead of running to God…
you run further away.

That voice says:
“You’re already too far gone.”

So you stop praying.
You stop showing up.
You slowly disappear from the presence of God.

So pride rises.
Submission fades.
And suddenly, your feelings outrank Scripture.
You start editing God’s Word to fit your lifestyle.
you’ve made yourself your own god.
That was the serpent’s first strategy.
but to distort the voice she trusted.
Because if he can corrupt the voice you follow…
he can control the life you live.
But here’s where it gets dangerous.
Some of you think the voice is yours.
You’ve lived with it so long…
Let Scripture cut through the confusion:
“My sheep hear My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me.” — John 10:27
Jesus didn’t say His sheep hear many voices.
So if the voice you’re listening to is pulling you away from Him…
If it feeds fear more than faith…
If it condemns you without pointing you back to grace…
Because the voice of Jesus does something different.
but it doesn’t trap you in it either.
“There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” — Romans 8:1
But here’s the truth we don’t like:

You cannot experience that freedom…
while clinging to the wrong voice.
This is where the Gospel steps in.
You and I—we’ve all listened to the wrong voice.

We chose sin.
We justified it.
We hid in it.
“All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
But God didn’t leave us there.
He didn’t just shout correction from heaven.

every lie you believed…
every sin you hid…
every voice that chained you—
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Not when you cleaned yourself up.
Not when you figured it out.
Still listening to the wrong voice.
Jesus didn’t die just to forgive you.
To break the authority of every voice that isn’t His.
Because the wrong voice always ends in death—
but the voice of Christ leads to life.
So now the question is not:
Because one voice will lead you deeper into hiding.
And one voice is calling you out of the grave.
Right now… you can feel it.
That quiet conviction rising in your chest.
Turn from the voices that have been shaping your life.
You don’t need to fix everything first.
“Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.” — Hebrews 3:15
will determine the life you live.
If this hit your heart, don’t ignore it.
